title: The Bridge: start the day with decisions
excerpt: A place to see what matters, inspect the evidence and direct the work. How Hyperdrift's Bridge connects an operator to a fleet of products—and where the same pattern fits another business.
shareLine: The useful morning brief ends with a decision you can make.

proof.description: Our internal Bridge connects product signals, decisions and recorded work.
proof.label: Read the technical account

image.alt: A previously published view of the Hyperdrift Bridge.
image.caption: The Bridge: a historical view of the operating interface, not current fleet results.

title: Give your agents the knowledge your best work depends on
excerpt: A useful agent needs your standards, examples and stopping points. Our publishing workflow shows how specialist knowledge becomes instructions people can inspect and improve.
shareLine: Write down what good work requires before asking an agent to do it.

proof.description: The anniversary article brings the writing, film and source ledger together.
proof.label: Explore the published example

media.alt: The title frame of the Hyperdrift anniversary film.
media.caption: The published anniversary film: one artefact supported by our editorial practice.

image.caption: Our publishing workflow in practice: the anniversary article and film.

title: Give an agent enough authority to finish its job
excerpt: Helm separates diagnosis from action and confines disruptive operations to drill services. The demonstration makes agent authority visible, inspectable and worth discussing before deployment.
shareLine: Useful delegation gives an agent a job, a boundary and a way to prove completion.

proof.description: Helm makes agent roles and restricted actions visible in a recorded sandbox drill.
proof.label: Watch the Helm demonstration

media.caption: Helm: recorded demonstration of agent roles and sandbox recovery.

image.alt: Four steps in agent delegation: route, inspect, act within scope, verify.
image.caption: The delegation pattern explained below. Watch the actual Helm drill in the working example.

title: A useful brief tells you who needs you next
excerpt: Standup reads public GitHub activity and returns a short, evidenced set of priorities. Its ordering rule shows what makes an AI brief useful enough to act on.
shareLine: A brief earns its place when you can act on it and check why.

proof.description: Standup turns public GitHub activity into a brief with evidence beside each recommendation.
proof.label: Try Standup

media.caption: Standup is a public project. Its historical example output is linked in the article.

title: Talk through the decision. Keep the evidence in view.
excerpt: Our First Officer prototype explores a conversation that moves the Bridge to the subject being discussed. HyperVideoMesh shows a related principle: the agent's work should remain visible and editable.
shareLine: A conversation becomes useful when both sides can point to the same thing.

proof.description: First Officer explores conversation over the Bridge. HyperVideoMesh provides a recorded example of inspectable agent edits.
proof.label: Watch the editing example

media.caption: HyperVideoMesh: a recorded creative-tool prototype. This is supporting evidence, not a First Officer recording.

image.caption: HyperVideoMesh illustrates visible agent edits. The First Officer voice prototype discussed here still needs a current recording.

title: Give your agent access to the work already on screen
excerpt: uk.gov Radar lets a browser agent work with the same shortlist its user sees. A concrete example of integrating AI into an existing workflow while keeping decisions visible.
shareLine: The agent and the person should work from the same state.
